messages:
Tom Chen: Hey team, we started getting 429s in production around 2025-11-12T00:40:07Z. Error body says rate_limit_exceeded and quota_type=rpm. Our telemetry shows a sharp spike from mobile clients — roughly 250 qps for ~30s, then traffic dropped but 429s persisted for a few minutes. Sample request_id: rid_abc123. Can someone help triage?

Ava: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste raw response headers (esp. X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After) and the API key id (partial obfuscated ok)? Also which region/endpoint were calls targeting?

Tom Chen: Region: us-east-1. API key: sk-live-xx...89. Example response headers we captured:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 00:41:07 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 00:45:00
Retry-After: 15
X-Request-ID: rid_abc123
Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","quota_type":"rpm","message":"request rate exceeded"}

Ravi: That Limit header is per-minute (rpm). Remaining=0 — looks like the token hit its RPM cap. Two quick checks from our side: 1) confirm whether this is token-scoped or org/realm cap, and 2) whether there was a fanout from many client IPs.

Maya: Remember we enforce both short-window burst gates and long-window quotas. 250 qps for 30s will trip short-window protections even if minute-average is marginal. Our token buckets map RPM to a per-second refill and short-window smoothing can drop tokens faster.

Tom Chen: Understood. We had the client pool scale aggressively after a push notification. Is there a safe repro we can run in staging to observe the behavior and validate mitigation?

Ava: Repro steps (staging):
1) Use a test key or staging project key.
2) Run a ramp script to mimic your spike (example: ~250 qps for 30s).
3) Collect response headers and the client-side logs.
Example curl loop to approximate 250 qps for 30s on Linux:
for i in $(seq 1 7500); do
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-xxxx" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" &
  sleep 0.004
done
wait

Ravi: When running, include -D - to capture headers and add a unique X-Request-Id per call so we can correlate. I'll start pulling ratecap counters for sk-live-xx...89 and search for rid_abc prefixes.

Maya: To specifically trip short-window circuit try a tighter burst: e.g., 1000 requests spread over 5s across multiple worker hosts. We have a node/go example we can share if needed.

Tom Chen: We also have an immediate retry loop in the client for 429s (no jitter). Could that be aggravating things?

Ravi: Absolutely — immediate retries compound the overload. Swap to exponential backoff with full jitter. Recommended pattern: initial 200ms, multiplier 2, max 5s, full jitter (0..delay), and a retry cap (3). That prevents cascading retries.

Ava: Are you on Hosted or Dedicated? Dedicated tenants sometimes have different burst limits. If Hosted, you can view token-level spikes in Console -> Usage -> API keys.

Tom Chen: We're Hosted. Console shows a spike to ~14k req/min at 00:40 (matches the timing). We need quick mitigations to reduce customer impact.

Maya: Quick mitigations: implement edge rate limiting (app-level token bucket), add ingress buffering to smooth bursts, ensure jittered retries on clients, and consider a temporary quota bump by opening a support request with traffic profiles and RIDs.

Ravi: On our side I opened a counters dump and started correlating logs for the API key and the request ids you shared. Please paste 3-5 more failed request ids to speed lookup.

Tom Chen: More ids: rid_abc124, rid_abc130, rid_abc198. Our worker concurrency spiked from ~25 to ~200 during the incident.

Ravi: Got them — I see those ids in the auth proxy and ratecap traces. The token for sk-live-xx...89 peaked at ~14,200 req/min (~237 rps) at 00:40, about 4x the configured RPM. Short-window gating fired and retries caused a ~15s throttling cascade.

Tom Chen: Do you use sliding windows or fixed-minute buckets? Our internal metrics aggregated by minute masked the sub-minute burst.

Maya: We use a token-bucket refill (sliding behavior). Short bursts draw down the bucket quickly; a second-high qps spike can exhaust it even if the minute average seems ok. We'll provide a short doc detailing the exact semantics.

Ava: Action items:
- Tom: deploy jittered backoff + ingress smoothing; roll to small percent of traffic first. (Owner: Tom)
- Support: opened ticket RINF-2025-784 for a temporary RPM increase; we'll pass along needed traffic details. (Owner: Ava)
- SRE: Ravi to post the counters and timeline once correlation is complete. (Owner: Ravi)
- Runtime: Maya to consider surfacing a clearer header to indicate short-window burst gating. (Owner: Maya)

Maya: Possible header UX improvement: add X-RateLimit-Burst to distinguish short-window gating from long-window RPM hits. If product agrees, we can prototype and document.

Ravi: Note for future triage: response body includes quota_type (rpm/tpm) and sometimes quota_scope (key/realm) when applicable. That field is helpful to know whether this is token or realm-level enforcement.

Tom Chen: Quick follow-up — after we pushed jittered retries and a small ingress buffer, errors dropped dramatically within a couple minutes. Console shows post-mitigation peak req/min down ~60%. Will keep monitoring and report back if anything persists.

Ava: Great, I'll keep RINF-2025-784 open for 24h for monitoring. Thanks for the quick updates! :thumbsup:
